title: A deduxit rule file
description: A calculus given as data: sorts, connectives, the zones of a sequent, schematic variables and rules. deduxit checks a derivation against it by matching. The schema covers the file's shape; deduxit also checks that every name is declared, every pattern well sorted, and every rule's contexts told apart.

version.description: The wire level of the document: 15.

name.description: The calculus's name, which a derivation names.

description.description: What the calculus is, for a reader.

sorts.description: The sorts beside `formula`, which every calculus has: for example `label` and `judgement` in a labelled calculus.

connectives.description: The connectives terms and patterns are built with.

sequent.description: The zones of a sequent, in the order written.

variables.description: The schematic variables, by sort: each stands for a term of that sort.

contexts.description: The context variables: each stands for what a zone holds beyond the members a rule writes out.

rules.description: The rules. Their names are distinct.

arity.description: How many terms the connective takes: 255 at most.

sorts.description: The sorts of its arguments, then the sort of the term it makes: one more entry than its arity. Without the key all are `formula`.

symbol.description: What is printed for it, where that is not its name.

fixity.description: Where it is printed among its arguments.

precedence.description: How tightly it binds when printed: a higher number binds tighter.

associativity.description: How a chain of it is read without brackets.

name.description: The zone's name, a key of every schematic sequent. `discharges` is taken.

sort.description: The sort of its members; `formula` where absent.

discipline.description: A set has neither multiplicity nor order, a multiset no order, a sequence both.

mark.description: What is written before the zone, as `⊢`.

least.description: The fewest members the zone holds.

most.description: The most members the zone holds.

pattern.description: A declared variable or a connective without arguments, by name; or an array of a connective's name and the patterns it is applied to. As an entry of a zone it may also be a context variable, alone or as the one argument of a unary connective (`["!", "Γ"]`: every member of the context under `!`). Nested 64 deep at most.

sequent.description: A schematic sequent: the entries of each zone, by the zone's name. An absent zone is empty.

premise.description: A schematic sequent, and under `discharges` the hypotheses the premise discharges, each a sequent of written members without contexts.

premises.description: The premises, in order; absent for a rule without any.

fresh.description: Variables matched by atoms that occur neither in the conclusion nor in a hypothesis in force: an eigenvariable, a new label.
